label: prf:per-nucleon-shift-additive-linearity
title: Proof of per nucleon shift additive linearity
html:
Proof. Proof of per nucleon shift additive linearity

Proof

The per-new-nucleon increment is invariant in 6 transitions (A : 2 \to 3, A : 3 \to 4, etc.) for both proton and neutron additions, regardless of starting atom (witness §1). This linearity identifies the closed form by induction:

  • Base case: \mathrm{shift}(D) = 40 = 18 \cdot 1 + 21 \cdot 1 + 1.
  • Step (+proton): \mathrm{shift}(Z+1, N) = \mathrm{shift}(Z, N) + 18 = 18(Z+1) + 21N + 1.
  • Step (+neutron): \mathrm{shift}(Z, N+1) = \mathrm{shift}(Z, N) + 21 = 18Z + 21(N+1) + 1.

The base-case +1 originates from the single mixed (p, n) interface in pppnnn ordering, contributing \alpha((\sigma+\sigma^{-1})/2) = 1 from the compound-shift theorem. This matches prop:alpha-shift-torus-knot's simplest interface case \alpha = 1 for the Hecke-symmetric average. \square

Generator-decomposition reading of (18, 21)

Each new generator's DP-max contribution to the q=0 pole is 1 (the canonical formalism), so DP-max increment per new nucleon is 12. The actual pole increments are:

  • per-new-proton: pole +9 (cancellation = 12 - 9 = 3), shift = 2 \cdot 9 = 18.
  • per-new-neutron: pole +10.5 (cancellation = 1.5, half-integer), shift = 2 \cdot 10.5 = 21.

Categorical verification (proton + deuteron)

Both the per-proton coefficient 18 and the multi-nucleon combination 18 + 21 + 1 = 40 are verified by direct symbolic Hoefsmit pole-order analysis:

  • Proton (A = 1, H_3): the canonical formalism (witness: per-irrep-pole-proton-h3.witness.json) computes \chi^\lambda_q(\mathcal{B}_p) for each \lambda \vdash 3 via the Hoefsmit seminormal, sums \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_p) = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda(q) \chi^\lambda_q(\mathcal{B}_p) with the canonical Wenzl Jones-Markov weights, substitutes q = u^2 (per the D(u) convention from the canonical formalism) and reports \mathrm{ord}_{u=0}(\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{B}_p)) = 19, matching 18 \cdot 1 + 21 \cdot 0 + 1 exactly.
  • Deuteron (A = 2, H_6): the canonical formalism (witness: per-irrep-pole-deuteron-h6.witness.json) uses three optimisations to make the symbolic H_6 analysis tractable: (a) cached symbolic y_\lambda(q) from y-lambda-wenzl-bridge-symbolic-witness.json (skips the >5 min solve_y_lambda(6) bottleneck), (b) cached symbolic \chi^\lambda_q(\beta_D) in chi-deuteron-h6.witness.json (first-run ~131 s, then <1 s), (c) per-term \mathrm{ord}_{u=0}(y_\lambda \cdot \chi^\lambda) analysis. The per-term maximum is uniquely 40 at \lambda = (4, 1, 1) (next-highest 39 at (4, 2)); since the maximum is unique, lower-order terms cannot cancel it, so \mathrm{ord}_{u=0}(\mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_D)) = 40 = 18 \cdot 1 + 21 \cdot 1 + 1 rigorously.

Reading note. The per-irrep maximum \mathrm{ord}_{q=0}^{(-)}\chi^\lambda_q(\mathcal{B}_p) = 11 (at \lambda = (2, 1)); the "18" in the formula is the per-proton additive coefficient of the full summed u-pole order of \mathrm{tr}_M, NOT the q-pole order of any single per-irrep \chi^\lambda_q.

The cancellation count enumerates the \sigma^2-relation reductions (\sigma^2 = h\sigma + 1 in the Hecke quadratic) in the new nucleon's intrinsic \sigma^{\pm 1}-adjacencies plus its incoming interface contribution.
